header:
Date: 2026-03-09 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m
Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Evan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (CISO - Triton), Priya Gupta (Eng Mgr - Triton), Carlos Vega (SRE - Triton)
summary: Intro discovery focused on Triton Finance's security requirements for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: SOC 2 / ISO attestations, SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC, audit logging and retention, encryption/BYOK/KMS, data residency and retention/deletion. Agreed next step: share compliance docs and schedule infra deep dive.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
00:00 Evan Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 55, 57 minutes scheduled. quick intros?
00:08 Mark Reynolds: Hi it's Mark, CISO at Triton Finance. head of security ops, happy to kick off.
00:13 Priya Gupta: Priya here, eng manager, i'll be owners for integration side.
00:17 Carlos Vega: Carlos, SRE, I support infra and networking.
00:21 Evan Morales: Great, Evan from Redwood, and Priya Shah our SE will run the technical details. real quick agenda - run through security posture, answer your questions, agree next steps.
00:31 Priya Shah: yep, and we'll be candid about hosted vs dedicated vs private - tradeoffs on latency/cost/security.
00:38 Mark Reynolds: Good. high level - we are evaluating a few providers. primary requirements are SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 - we need to see the reports, and we have to support SSO via SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and we need strong audit logs with at least 12 months retention. also BYOK or customer-managed keys is a hard ask for us.
01:00 Priya Shah: understood. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant and we have ISO 27001 attestation - i'll share the relevant reports after this call. for KMS we support bring-your-own-key for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys in some tiers via KMS integration and we can discuss HSM options.
01:19 Carlos Vega: For hosted, is the key material stored by Redwood or do we hold it in our cloud KMS? like can we rotate without Redwood involvement?
01:28 Priya Shah: good q - for Hosted we support envelope encryption where you provision a KMS key in your cloud account (BYOK) and we only hold the wrapped key, rotation can be initiated by you. for Dedicated/Private you get more isolation and you can use your HSM. i will share the KMS integration guide.
01:49 Mark Reynolds: Audit logs - are logs immutable? what about access to raw logs? we need to feed into our SIEM (Splunk).
01:58 Priya Shah: we stream audit logs via secure syslog or S3 export; logs include API calls, route-level usage, and admin events. retention is configurable; out of the box 90 days on Hosted, but for enterprise we can arrange 12 months (or longer) - for Dedicated/Private customers we host logs in your VPC or you pull them to your SIEM.
02:22 Carlos Vega: is there tamper evidence? we need write-once or some integrity checks.
02:27 Priya Shah: we use append-only audit stores with immutability flags and SHA-based checksums internally; for high-assurance needs we support pushing signed logs into your S3 bucket with object lock if required.
02:40 Mark Reynolds: ok. data residency - we have EU customers, need data at rest in eu-west-1 for certain tenants. what controls do you have?
02:50 Evan Morales: Redwood routes requests by region; Hosted supports region pinning and we can ensure model inference runs in eu-west-1. for Dedicated/Private you can deploy in our EU region or on-prem. We'll need to discuss traffic egress and cross-region backups.
03:05 Priya Gupta: any SOC2 scope details - does Redwood include machine learning infra, models, logs? we need to know what is in-scope and what you consider third-party.
03:13 Priya Shah: good point - SOC 2 covers our control plane, hosted inference runtime, storage for customer data in-scope, and supporting services. we can share the trust center doc that maps in-scope systems. third-party dependencies like cloud provider have their own attestations which we reference.
03:26 Mark Reynolds: SSO - we'll likely use Okta. support for SAML 2.0 and SCIM is required for us; SCIM for provisioning and deprovisioning. also need session inactivity timeouts and support for MFA enforcement.
03:38 Priya Shah: yes we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning on both Hosted and Dedicated. RBAC: we have built-in roles (Admin, Developer, Viewer) and you can create custom roles via the console or API. for SSO we can map SAML attributes to roles, and you can enforce JIT provisioning or block sign-ins for non-member domains.
04:00 Carlos Vega: On Dedicated, how isolated is the compute? is it multi-tenant on the same GPU cluster? we need assurance there is no KV cache leakage between tenants.
04:10 Priya Shah: Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation primitives - compute may be on shared hardware in some configs but we use hardware tenancy options and strong kernel isolation; KV cache is namespace-isolated per tenant and scrubbed between workloads. for highest assurance Private/on-prem provides physical isolation.
04:32 Mark Reynolds: ok. can you summarize the differences quickly for a non-technical exec?
04:37 Evan Morales: sure - Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, lower upfront cost, and is great for non-sensitive workloads; Dedicated provides reserved capacity, stronger isolation, and SLA-backed latency; Private is customer-managed network or on-premises for regulated data - more control, higher ops overhead. security-wise, BYOK and HSM support improve as you move from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.
04:58 Priya Gupta: encryption in transit and at rest - are models, KV cache, and logs encrypted at rest?
05:04 Priya Shah: yes - TLS for in transit; at rest we encrypt models, KV caches, and artifacts using AES-256. keys are managed by KMS (cloud KMS or customer KMS). for ephemeral caches we apply additional memory protections and in some modes we zero memory on release.
05:22 Mark Reynolds: What about data retention and deletion - we need the ability to purge logs and user data on demand to satisfy data subject requests.
05:30 Priya Shah: we provide APIs to delete customer data and you can request a verified purge. retention policies can be set per route/namespace and we log deletion events in audit logs. for Hosted we have standard retention windows but for enterprise we can customize.
05:47 Carlos Vega: any certifications for cryptographic modules - do you support FIPS or HSM vendors?
05:53 Priya Shah: we integrate with cloud HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM) and support FIPS-compliant modules where the provider exposes them. for Private/on-prem you can bring your own HSM.
06:05 Mark Reynolds: incident response - do you share notifications and forensic artifacts? what's SLA for incident notification?
06:11 Evan Morales: we have an incident response policy; for customers with enterprise contracts we commit to notify within 24 hours of detection for high-severity incidents, provide root cause analysis, and share relevant logs and timelines. we'll include contact points in the agreement.
06:25 Priya Gupta: network requirements - firewall rules, egress IPs, static IPs for allowlisting?
06:31 Priya Shah: we publish IP ranges for Hosted; Dedicated can be deployed into your VPC with private peering and static egress IPs. Private is under your control. we'll share network diagrams and required ports.
06:46 Mark Reynolds: legal and data processing addendum - our legal team will need DPA + data residency clauses and potentially subprocessor lists.
06:53 Evan Morales: yes, we provide a standard DPA and subprocessor list. for enterprise we can negotiate addenda and include specific residency clauses.
07:02 Carlos Vega: performance/benchmarks - if we do encryption and BYOK, is there an observable latency penalty?
07:08 Priya Shah: minimal for envelope encryption; KMS calls are cached, and we use local wrapping keys for the runtime to avoid per-request KMS latency. there is a small overhead but we've benchmarked for typical seq lengths - we'll share benchmark sheets.
07:24 Mark Reynolds: any history of penetration tests or third-party assessments?
07:29 Priya Shah: we run annual pen tests and will share executive summaries; we also have bug bounty program details.
07:36 Priya Gupta: curious about model privacy - do models see raw data and is there any training on customer prompts?
07:43 Priya Shah: we do not train on customer data by default. customer data is not used to update our public models unless explicitly opted in under an agreement. for Hosted we have options to opt out of any data usage. we'll include the policy doc.
07:57 Evan Morales: looks like we're converging on items to share. quick recap then next steps.
08:02 Evan Morales: Redwood to send SOC 2 + ISO certs, KMS/BYOK doc, network diagram, pen test summary, and pricing options. Triton will confirm Okta test tenant and in-scope systems list.
08:12 Mark Reynolds: yeah i'll get legal and infra contacts and will drop them in the thread.
08:16 Carlos Vega: we'll want to schedule the infra deep dive with our networking folks - prefer week of Mar 16.
08:20 Priya Shah: i'll send calendar invite options for Mar 16 and include a checklist for what to have ready (VPC CIDRs, proxy info, SIEM endpoint).
08:29 Evan Morales: perfect. thanks everyone; we'll follow up via email with the docs and next steps.
08:34 Mark Reynolds: thanks, bye.
08:36 Priya Gupta: thanks bye.
08:37 (call ends)

Notes: transcription has some noise, speaker overlap occasionally misattributed. The call included explicit asks for SOC 2/ISO artifacts, KMS/BYOK details, SAML + SCIM support, RBAC mapping, audit log immutability and exports, data residency and retention/deletion APIs, network diagrams and firewall/eGRESS requirements. Agreed to schedule infra deep dive week of 2026-03-16 and for Redwood to provide compliance docs and integration guides.
